title: Daily climate explained at most about one third of multi-decadal runoff-efficiency changes at south-east Australian gauges (1889-2021); adjusted efficiency fell in two steps, near 1957 and 2010
abstract: Question: south-east Australian (SE-AU) runoff at equal annual rain was about 20% above the 1957-1996 relation before 1957 and 15% below it in 2010-2021. Is this multi-decadal change in runoff efficiency caused by climate that annual rain does not show (rain seasonality, daily intensity, wet days, rain sequences, evaporative demand)? Approach: we drove two daily rainfall-runoff models with fixed parameters (GR4J, SIMHYD) with CAMELS-AUS daily SILO climate from 1889 at 50 long-record gauges (31 SE-AU, 19 northern control; Water Data Online flow). For each gauge, Q = a + bP + cP(t-1) was fitted on 1957-1996 to observed flow (D_obs) and to simulated flow (climate-implied D_clim); D_res = D_obs - D_clim is the climate-adjusted departure. 2-degree cell bootstrap. Plan written before any model run. Results (SE-AU): before 1957, D_obs was +22.6% (95% CI 12.6 to 29.6; 20 gauges) but D_clim only +4.3% (GR4J) and +7.1% (SIMHYD). In 2010-2021, D_obs was -15.0% (-24.5 to -9.0) and D_clim -1.7% and -3.2%. The post-drought contrast (2010-2021 minus 1946-1955) was -36.9 points observed and -2.4 from climate. Climate explained about half of the WWII/Millennium drought contrast (Millennium Drought had 15% fewer wet days) and 46% of the variance of 13-year group departures before 1997. The result held with AGCD rain, with climatological PET, with calibration on all pre-1997 years and without regulated gauges (climate share 4-34% across models and variants). Post hoc, the climate-adjusted series of 21 fixed gauges had three levels: +14.8% before 1957, -0.9% in 1957-2009, -12.9% after 2010 (breaks 1957 and 2010; same with calibration on all pre-1997 years). The Millennium Drought decade itself had only -3.6%. Northern gauges had a non-climatic fall near 1964-1978 and did not recover; their apparent recovery after 2009 was climatic. The IPO Tripole Index and PDO did not track the observed or adjusted efficiency (r -0.01 to 0.21). Conclusion: the multi-decadal efficiency change is mostly not climatic in this sense; after adjustment, efficiency fell in two steps rather than oscillating. The causes of both steps remain open (catchment change or flow measurement). By the planned rule the result is 'not climatic' with all gauges and 'partly climatic' by a small margin without the diverted gauge 410033. Limitations: two conceptual models; few pre-1957 gauges (20); early ratings unknown; sparse early rain network; step analysis post hoc.
